proofs.proof_tex:
For an \(\epsilon\)-differentially private Markov kernel \(T\), write
\[
 {cal R}(T,P)=
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n},T}|T(D_n)-\theta(P)|.
\]
All constants below depend only on
\(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\).  They never depend on
\(n\) or \(\epsilon\).

First, privacy cannot reduce minimax risk.  Define the conditional
barycenter
\[
 \bar T(D_n)=\int_{[-2,2]}t\,T(dt\mid D_n).
\]
The bounded output support makes \(\bar T\) a measurable, nonprivate
estimator taking values in \([-2,2]\).  Since the absolute value is convex,
conditional Jensen's inequality gives, for every \(P\in\mathcal M_H\),
\[
 |\bar T(D_n)-\theta(P)|
 \le \int |t-\theta(P)|\,T(dt\mid D_n).
\]
Using the sampling law in \(\mathrm{ass:iid}\), taking expectations and
then the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal M_H\) yields
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}{\cal R}(T,P)
 \ge \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}|\bar T(D_n)-\theta(P)|
 \ge R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},                                      \tag{1}
\]
where the last inequality is the definition
\(\mathrm{def:nonprivate-risk}\).  Taking the infimum in (1) over the
private kernels in \(\mathrm{def:private-risk}\) proves
\(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\).

We next prove the dense-cell branch.  Fix a nonnegative
\(C^\infty\) function \(g\), supported in \((-1,1)^d\), with
\(g(0)=1\).  For \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), let
\[
 h=c_h\delta^{1/\gamma},\qquad
 g_h(x)=g((x-x_0)/h),
\]
where \(c_h>0\) and \(\delta_0>0\) are fixed and sufficiently small.
Because \(x_0\in[1/4,3/4]^d\), this support is contained in
\([0,1]^d\).  The elementary scaling identity for derivatives and the
Hölder remainder gives
\[
 \|\delta g_h\|_{\mathcal H^\gamma}
 \le C_g\delta h^{-\gamma}=C_gc_h^{-\gamma}.
\]
Choose \(c_h\) so the last constant is at most \(L\), reducing
\(\delta_0\) if necessary to retain the support condition.

Define two full-data laws \(P_0,P_1\) as follows.  Under both laws,
\(X\) is uniform, \(A\mid X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), and
\(\mu_0=0\).  Put \(\tau_0=0\) and
\(\tau_1=\delta g_h\).  Given \(X=x\), draw potential outcomes in
\(\{-1,1\}\) with respective means \(0\) and \(\tau_j(x)\), independently
of \(A\), and set \(Y=AY_1+(1-A)Y_0\).  Thus consistency and conditional
exchangeability hold by construction.  The propensity equals \(1/2\), so
uniform overlap holds because \(e_0\le1/4\); the propensity and control
regression are in their declared Hölder balls because they are constant;
and the preceding scaling bound puts the effect in
\(\mathcal H^\gamma(L)\).  Hence \(P_0,P_1\in\mathcal M_H\) by
\(\mathrm{def:holder-class}\), and
\[
 \theta(P_1)-\theta(P_0)=\delta g_h(x_0)=\delta.              \tag{2}
\]

Couple the two records by using the same \(X,A\), and use a common uniform
random variable to couple the two binary conditional outcome laws.  The
conditional mismatch probability for binary laws with means \(m_0,m_1\)
is \(|m_1-m_0|/2\).  Therefore one coordinate mismatches with probability
\[
 \frac14\int_{[0,1]^d}|\delta g_h(x)|\,dx
 \le C\delta h^d.                                           \tag{3}
\]
Repeating this coupling independently over the \(n\) coordinates gives a
coupling of \(P_0^{\otimes n}\) and \(P_1^{\otimes n}\) with
\[
 D_G:=\mathbb E d_{\mathrm{Ham}}(D_n,D_n')
 \le Cn\delta h^d
 \le Cn\delta^{1+d/\gamma}.                                \tag{4}
\]
Since \(n\epsilon\ge1\), the cap in \(\rho_G\) is inactive and
\(\rho_G^{1+d/\gamma}=(n\epsilon)^{-1}\).  Set
\(\delta=a_G\rho_G\), where \(a_G>0\) is a sufficiently small fixed
constant.  Then \(\delta\le\delta_0\) and (4) gives
\[
 \epsilon D_G\le Ca_G^{1+d/\gamma}.                         \tag{5}
\]

For any private estimator \(T\), the midpoint rule
\(\varphi_T=\mathbf 1\{T\ge\delta/2\}\) is pure
\(\epsilon\)-differentially private by post-processing.  The two singleton
hypothesis classes and (4) meet the premises of
\(\mathrm{lem:private-le-cam-coupling}\), with privacy slack zero.  Choose
\(a_G\) so that the right side of (5) is at most \(1/10\).  The cited lemma
then bounds the equal-prior testing error below by a universal positive
constant \(c_0\).  On each testing error the absolute estimation loss is at
least \(\delta/2\), by (2).  Consequently
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}{\cal R}(T,P)
 \ge \frac12\{{\cal R}(T,P_0)+{\cal R}(T,P_1)\}
 \ge \frac{\delta}{2}c_0.
\]
Taking the infimum over \(T\) proves
\[
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge c_G\rho_G.                 \tag{6}
\]

It remains to establish the sparse-collision branch.  Suppose first that
\(\rho_F\ge\rho_G\).  Again the caps are inactive under
\(n\epsilon\ge1\), and, with
\(D_F=1+d/\gamma+d/q\),
\[
 \rho_F^{D_F}=(n^2\epsilon)^{-1},\qquad
 \rho_G^{1+d/\gamma}=(n\epsilon)^{-1}.                      \tag{7}
\]
We claim that \(n\rho_F^{d/q}\le1\).  Otherwise, (7) would imply
\[
 \rho_F^{1+d/\gamma}
 =\frac{\rho_F^{D_F}}{\rho_F^{d/q}}
 <\frac{1/(n^2\epsilon)}{1/n}
 =\rho_G^{1+d/\gamma},
\]
and hence \(\rho_F<\rho_G\), a contradiction.

Set \(\delta=a_F\rho_F\),
\(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\), and
\(\ell\asymp\delta^{1/q}\).  By the preceding claim,
\[
 n\ell^d\le C a_F^{d/q}n\rho_F^{d/q}\le C a_F^{d/q}.        \tag{8}
\]
Choose \(a_F>0\) small enough that (8) is at most the constant required by
\(\mathrm{lem:two-fiber-distance-certificate}\), and also so that
\(\delta\) is in that lemma's small-separation range.  The lemma then
constructs smooth shared-sign priors supported on laws in
\(\mathcal M_H\), with target values \(\delta\) and zero, respectively,
whose prior-predictive samples have a coupling satisfying
\[
 D_F^{\mathrm{coup}}
 \le C\delta n^2h^d\ell^d
 \le Cn^2\delta^{1+d/\gamma+d/q}
 =Cn^2\delta^{D_F}.                                        \tag{9}
\]
Equations (7) and (9) give
\[
 \epsilon D_F^{\mathrm{coup}}
 \le C\epsilon n^2a_F^{D_F}\rho_F^{D_F}
 =Ca_F^{D_F}.                                               \tag{10}
\]
Thresholding at \(\delta/2\) again produces a pure-private test.  Apply
\(\mathrm{lem:private-le-cam-coupling}\) to the two prior predictives and
choose \(a_F\) still smaller so that (10) is at most \(1/10\).  The test
error is bounded below by a fixed positive constant, and averaging risk
over each prior gives
\[
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge c_F\delta
 \ge c_F'\rho_F.                                           \tag{11}
\]
If \(\rho_F<\rho_G\), (6) directly implies (11), after decreasing the
constant.

Equations (1), (6), and (11) bound the private risk below by fixed positive
multiples of \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\), \(\rho_G\), and \(\rho_F\),
respectively.  Taking the smallest of these constants proves
\[
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
 \ge c_{\mathrm{lower}}
 \{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\},
\]
including every support, overlap, smoothness, occupancy, and privacy regime
condition stated in the theorem.

added_lemmas.statement:
The exact-uniform class is a strict subclass of the bounded-density class,
\(\mathcal M_H\subsetneq\mathcal P_K\), and for every \(n\) and
\(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP},K}\ge R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M_H\).  By \(\mathrm{def:holder-class}\), consistency,
conditional exchangeability, overlap, the three stated Hölder conditions,
and \(q<\gamma\) all hold.  By \(\mathrm{ass:uniform-design}\),
\(P_X\) has Lebesgue density identically equal to one.  Since
\(0<e_0\le1/4\),
\[
 e_0\le 1\le e_0^{-1}.
\]
Thus every condition in
\(\mathrm{def:kennedy-bounded-density-class}\) holds, proving
\(\mathcal M_H\subseteq\mathcal P_K\).

The inclusion is strict.  Choose \(t=1/4\) and define the density
\[
 f^\dagger(x)=1+t(2x_1-1),\qquad x\in[0,1]^d.
\]
It integrates to one, because
\(\int_0^1(2u-1)\,du=0\), and it satisfies
\[
 3/4\le f^\dagger(x)\le5/4,
 \qquad e_0\le f^\dagger(x)\le e_0^{-1},
\]
where the second display uses \(e_0\le1/4\).  Let \(X\) have this density,
let \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of \(X\), set
\(Y_0=Y_1=0\), and impose consistency, so \(Y=0\).  Then
\(\pi=1/2\), \(\mu_0=0\), and \(\tau=0\).  These constant functions lie
in the required Hölder balls because \(L\ge2\); overlap holds; and
exchangeability and consistency hold by construction.  Hence the resulting
law \(P^\dagger\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_K\).  Its covariate density is
not constant, so \(P^\dagger\notin\mathcal M_H\) by
\(\mathrm{ass:uniform-design}\).  This proves strictness.

Finally, for every private kernel \(T\), set
\({\cal R}(T,P)=\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n},T}|T(D_n)-\theta(P)|\).  Set
inclusion gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_K}{\cal R}(T,P)
 \ge \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}{\cal R}(T,P).
\]
Taking the infimum over the same collection of pure
\(\epsilon\)-private kernels on both sides, as specified in
\(\mathrm{def:kennedy-private-risk}\) and
\(\mathrm{def:private-risk}\), proves
\[
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP},K}\ge
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}.
\]

added_lemmas.statement:
There is a constant \(c_K>0\), depending only on
\(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\), such that throughout \(n\epsilon\ge1\),
\[
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP},K}
 \ge c_K\left[
 \left\{n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}
 \vee n^{-2/(2+d/\gamma+d/q)}\right\}
 \vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\right].
\]
This is a converse transfer only; it asserts no upper bound over
\(\mathcal P_K\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{lem:exact-uniform-superclass-monotonicity}\) and
\(\mathrm{thm:full-class-lower-frontier}\),
\[
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP},K}
 \ge R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
 \ge c_{\mathrm{lower}}
 \{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\}.                 \tag{12}
\]
The proved nonprivate floor
\(\mathrm{lem:nonprivate-cate-rate-floor}\) supplies a constant
\(c_{\mathrm{NP}}>0\), depending on the same model parameters, for which
\[
 R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}
 \ge c_{\mathrm{NP}}
 \left\{n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}
 \vee n^{-2/(2+d/\gamma+d/q)}\right\}.                      \tag{13}
\]
Substituting (13) into (12), and using for nonnegative numbers
\(u,v,w\) and \(a>0\) the elementary inequality
\[
 (au)\vee v\vee w
 \ge (1\wedge a)(u\vee v\vee w),
\]
gives the asserted bound with
\(c_K=c_{\mathrm{lower}}(1\wedge c_{\mathrm{NP}})\).  Every lower branch
therefore transfers from the exact-uniform subclass to the larger
bounded-density class.  No step reverses the inclusion, so the argument
does not transfer any estimator or upper bound.
added_lemmas.justification: The exact-uniform lower construction is a valid subexperiment of the larger bounded-density Hölder class, so all nonprivate, dense-private, and sparse-private converse branches transfer upward without claiming an estimator on that larger class.
added_lemmas.gap: Kennedy et al. establish the nonprivate pointwise-CATE frontier on the bounded-density class but do not provide either pure-private lower branch.
added_lemmas.consumer: The result separates the unconditional superclass converse from the still-open exact-uniform matching upper bound.

proposed.name: Kennedy bounded-design-density Hölder class
proposed.construction:
Let \(\lambda_d\) denote Lebesgue measure on \([0,1]^d\).  Define
\[
\begin{split}
 \mathcal P_K=\{P:;&P\text{ is a law on }(X,A,Y_0,Y_1,Y),\quad
 P_X\ll\lambda_d,\quad
 e_0\le dP_X/d\lambda_d\le e_0^{-1}\quad\lambda_d\text{-a.e.},\\
 &Y=AY_1+(1-A)Y_0\quad P\text{-a.s.},\quad
 Y_a\perp A\mid X\quad(a=0,1),\\
 &e_0\le\pi(x)\le1-e_0,\quad
 \pi\in\mathcal H^\alpha(L),\quad
 \mu_0\in\mathcal H^\beta(L),\quad
 \tau\in\mathcal H^\gamma(L),\quad q=\alpha+\beta<\gamma\}.
\end{split}
\]
This is the bounded-design-density Hölder lower-bound class of Kennedy,
Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman, specialized to the common bounded
outcome support and constants used here.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This precisely declares the larger published bounded-density model to which the exact-uniform converse transfers.

proposed.name: Pure-private minimax risk over the bounded-density superclass

proposed_core_edits.reason: The new theorem must distinguish the superclass minimax risk from the existing exact-uniform risk.

proposed.statement:
There is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{lower}}>0\), depending only on
\(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\), such that throughout \(n\epsilon\ge1\),
\[
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
 \ge c_{\mathrm{lower}}\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\}.
\]
The \(\rho_G\) term is witnessed by a localized one-record subexperiment.
For the \(\rho_F\) term, whenever \(\rho_F\ge\rho_G\), there are smooth
shared-sign two-fiber mixtures in \(\mathcal M_H\), separated by
\(\delta\asymp\rho_F\), whose prior-predictive samples admit a coupling with
expected Hamming distance at most
\(C\delta n^2h^d\ell^d\), where
\(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\),
\(\ell\asymp\delta^{1/q}\), and \(n\ell^d\le C\).  If
\(\rho_F<\rho_G\), the \(\rho_F\) lower bound is already implied by the
\(\rho_G\) branch.
proposed.justification: A same-class converse determines whether dense occupancy creates a new privacy radius or merely activates the first-order branch.
proposed.gap: Kennedy et al. give only the nonprivate term, and Acharya et al. give generic coupling inequalities rather than the occupancy-indexed causal mixtures needed for the two privacy terms.
proposed.consumer: It prevents an upper mechanism from being certified against a surrogate regression class or only a sparse diagnostic family.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The revised sparse-branch proof invokes the already-proved two-fiber distance certificate, and the nonprivate monotonicity step invokes the nonprivate-risk definition directly; both dependencies must be explicit.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: Unconditionally, \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\gtrsim R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\) on \(\mathcal M_H\), and \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP},K}\gtrsim [n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\vee n^{-2/(2+d/\gamma+d/(\alpha+\beta))}]\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\) on \(\mathcal P_K\). The matching relation \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\) on \(\mathcal M_H\) is conditional on an affirmative full-fiber occupancy lift.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The existing unconditional equivalence is stale while the exact-uniform full-fiber upper construction remains unresolved; the replacement records the proved exact-uniform and superclass lower functionals and labels the equivalence as conditional.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 establish the nonprivate pointwise Hölder-CATE minimax rate on a bounded-design-density class, with the upper construction in Section 5.

proposed.comparator_claim: Section 4 uses treated--control occupancy and effect homogeneity to obtain a global nonprivate rate with a collision term.
The paper stabilizes central-private U-statistics using local Hájek projections and tuple reweighting.
Section 4 gives a general pure-private T-mechanism based on clipped likelihood-ratio tests and finite covers.
The paper gives central-private Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad inequalities based on expected Hamming transport.
Theorems 1 and 3 give finite-query and functional observational CATE releases under approximate differential privacy.
The sparse-histogram lower bound and compact dense-histogram theorem show that pure-private costs can change with representation and occupancy.
Theorems 1--2 and the adaptive lower bound characterize extra logarithmic costs for pointwise federated-private density adaptation.
The paper establishes nonprivate heterogeneous-effect minimax rates with explicit random-design geometry.
Definition 2 and Section 4 construct T-estimators from coherent tests on countable model nets.

prose_updates.tldr: The unconditional results are the exact occupancy-amplification identity and the sparse- and dense-cell pure-private lower branches on the exact-uniform Hölder class \(\mathcal M_H\). Since \(\mathcal M_H\) is a strict subclass of Kennedy et al.'s larger bounded-design-density class \(\mathcal P_K\), minimax monotonicity transfers the full converse, including the published nonprivate floor, to \(\mathcal P_K\). A matching upper bound on \(\mathcal M_H\) remains conditional on the unresolved full-fiber occupancy lift; no upper bound is transferred to \(\mathcal P_K\), and smoothness adaptation remains open with no adaptive rate or logarithmic penalty claimed.

project_justification.fill: The project proves the exact occupancy identity and the sparse and dense pure-private lower branches on the exact-uniform class, then transfers the complete converse upward to Kennedy et al.'s larger bounded-density class by subclass monotonicity. Matching attainment on the exact-uniform class still requires the unresolved nuisance-independent full-fiber score, and adaptation remains a separate open problem with no asserted penalty.

prose_updates.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman establish the nonprivate pointwise-CATE frontier on a larger bounded-design-density Hölder class. This work proves the occupancy identity and both pure-private lower branches on the strict exact-uniform subclass \(\mathcal M_H\); because every exact-uniform law is in Kennedy et al.'s class \(\mathcal P_K\), the nonprivate floor and both privacy converse branches transfer upward, but no upper bound does. Zeng et al. motivate conditioning on occupancy, Chaudhuri et al. motivate stable private projection statistics, and Acharya et al. supply the Hamming-coupling inequality used in the converse; none supplies the unresolved full-class CATE score. Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen provide multiscale and adaptive-lower-bound templates only for a separate open adaptation question, so no CATE adaptation rate or logarithmic penalty is claimed here. The remaining cited work concerns testing, approximate-private CATE release, sparse-versus-dense representations, and nonprivate random-design geometry rather than a matching pure-private upper frontier for this model.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The unconditional scope is fixed-smoothness inference under the exact-uniform design: the occupancy-amplification identity and both pure-private lower branches hold on \(\mathcal M_H\). The resulting converse transfers to Kennedy et al.'s larger bounded-density class \(\mathcal P_K\) solely by superclass monotonicity. The matching upper bound remains conditional and exact-uniform because the nuisance-independent full-fiber occupancy lift is unresolved; transfer of that upper bound to a bounded-density design is not claimed. Smoothness adaptation is a separate open question, with neither an adaptive rate nor a logarithmic penalty asserted.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem unconditionally certifies the nonprivate, dense-cell, and sparse-collision lower branches on the exact-uniform class; its superclass corollary then transfers every branch to the larger bounded-density model.
statement_notes.gap: Kennedy et al. provide the nonprivate term, while Acharya et al. provide a generic private coupling inequality; neither gives the exact-uniform shared-sign causal construction or the sparse-to-dense pure-private converse proved here.
statement_notes.consumer: The lower frontier benchmarks any future exact-uniform occupancy mechanism and, through subclass monotonicity, supplies a valid converse on Kennedy et al.'s larger class without asserting an upper transfer.
